minutes.headline: Planning Board put Highfield Village on the July 22 agenda, asking the developer for a chronology and milestones.
minutes.summary: The board heard committee reports, a school building update, and the planning director's report. Most of the time went to the long-extended Highfield Village subdivision, Emerald Place's shift from for-sale to lease-to-own, a possible marijuana dispensary bylaw, and how plans are distributed to board members. The captions show no formal votes beyond approving minutes and adjourning.

public_comment.topic: Explained the Sewer Commission is only discussing a sewer allocation with Highfield; no new plans submitted, and the Fitchburg IMA is entangled.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the Highfield Village extension request to July 22 and asked the developer's representative to bring a history of extensions and a milestone schedule.
Highfield Village was placed on the July 22 calendar.
A member reported the town is getting about half of the promised Chapter 90 state road funding increase, which works out to less than last year.
A member proposed charging developers for repeated extension requests; the planning director will share the existing fee schedule.
The planning director is to ask developers for PDF plans and send them to members, after consulting the IT director on shared document access.

why_it_matters: Repeated extensions on a long-running subdivision keep its approval open, and a fee for repeat requests would change what delay costs a developer.
Lower Chapter 90 funding than expected means less state money for local road repair, which can push road work toward the town budget, mostly taxes, or delay it.
watch_next: July 22 Planning Board meeting at Town Hall: Highfield Village extension request, with the extension history and milestone schedule.
The planning director's existing fee schedule, and the typed list of board goals, which is due to be taken up at the meeting after July 22.
